findings.reason: Untrusted source: gigaset_probe (drivers/isdn/gigaset/usb-gigaset.c:653) reads interface->cur_altsetting of a device that only has to match USB M105 VID/PID (0x0584:0x000D style check at lines 672-677), interfaceNumber==0, altsetting 0, and class 255; a malicious gadget with those IDs can declare bNumEndpoints=0 or 1. Missing guarantee: the file contains zero occurrences of bNumEndpoints (verified by grep), so endpoint[0] at line 708 and endpoint[1] at line 727 are indexed with no validation of the descriptor-declared count. Unsafe use: endpoint[0].desc.wMaxPacketSize sizes kmalloc bulk_out_buffer and programs the bulk-out pipe; endpoint[1].desc.wMaxPacketSize sizes kmalloc rcvbuf, and .bEndpointAddress/.bInterval program a submitted interrupt URB (usb_fill_int_urb at 737-741). With 0 endpoints the flex-array indexing reads past the allocated usb_host_interface (NULL/OOB read at plug-in, kernel crash at probe); with 1 endpoint the endpoint[1] read is an OOB descriptor read whose wMaxPacketSize/bInterval values propagate into URB buffer size and scheduling. Counterevidence checked: no bNumEndpoints or num_altsetting guard anywhere in usb-gigaset.c; the sibling bas-gigaset.c driver does check (line 2320), showing the missing check is not systemic.
findings.conclusion: gigaset_probe indexes endpoint[0]/endpoint[1] of an unvalidated descriptor array (no bNumEndpoints check in the file) to size buffers and program URBs; a 0/1-endpoint M105-spoofing gadget crashes probe or feeds OOB-read values into URB setup at plug-in.

findings.reason: Untrusted source: uea_bind (line 2529) runs at USB probe for devices matching the Analog Devices/Devolo Eagle ADSL VID/PID table; only interfaceNumber==0 (UEA_INTR_IFACE_NO) and the presence of interfaces 1/2 are checked, never the endpoint count. uea_bind calls uea_boot(sc) at line 2600, and uea_boot reads actconfig->interface[0]->altsetting[0].endpoint[0].desc.bInterval and submits the interrupt URB with it. Missing guarantee: no bNumEndpoints check anywhere in ueagle-atm.c (grep: only this one endpoint[ use); the descriptor count of interface 0 altsetting 0 is attacker-controlled. Unsafe use: with bNumEndpoints==0 the endpoint flex-array is empty and &endpoint[0].desc reads past the allocated descriptor array (OOB read at plug-in whose value becomes the interrupt URB interval); usb_maxpacket-style validation exists only for the bulk pipes in usbatm.c get_pipes-equivalent code, not for this endpoint[0] read. This is the same interrupt-URB endpoint[0].desc.bInterval pattern fact f009 proved for this file in s04, now confirmed present in s10 at lines 2209-2210. Counterevidence checked: usbatm.c core validates the bulk endpoints' maxpacket (lines 1104-1112) but nothing validates interface[0] altsetting[0] endpoint[0] before uea_boot.
findings.conclusion: uea_boot reads actconfig->interface[0]->altsetting[0].endpoint[0].desc.bInterval with no bNumEndpoints validation and submits an interrupt URB with it; a zero-endpoint interface-0 Eagle-spoofing gadget OOB-reads descriptor memory at modem bind (plug-in).

findings.reason: Untrusted source: usb_pcwd_probe (drivers/watchdog/pcwd_usb.c:606) reads interface->cur_altsetting of any device presenting the Berkshire PC watchdog product IDs whose interface class is USB_CLASS_HID (line 626); the endpoint array content is fully device-supplied. Missing guarantee: the file contains no bNumEndpoints check (grep verified: only this one endpoint[ occurrence), so endpoint[0] is indexed without validating the descriptor-declared count. Unsafe use: endpoint[0].desc is immediately dereferenced by usb_endpoint_is_int_in (line 636), then bEndpointAddress programs the interrupt pipe, wMaxPacketSize sets intr_size (min 8) for usb_alloc_coherent buffers and URBs. With bNumEndpoints==0 the indexing reads past the allocated usb_host_interface into unmapped/adjacent memory (OOB read or crash at plug-in), and any OOB-read bEndpointAddress/wMaxPacketSize flows into pipe setup and buffer sizing. Counterevidence checked: the only guard between probe and the read is the interface-class check; no usb_ifnum/num_altsetting/bNumEndpoints validation exists in the file.
findings.conclusion: usb_pcwd_probe indexes endpoint[0].desc with no bNumEndpoints check (only a HID-class check precedes) and feeds the read into usb_endpoint_is_int_in, pipe setup and URB buffer sizing; a zero-endpoint gadget OOB-reads descriptor memory at plug-in.

The serial core discovers endpoints by looping 'for (i = 0; i < iface_desc->desc.bNumEndpoints; ++i)' (lines 775-838) and fills per-type pointer tables, so drivers' later endpoint uses are count-bounded; the PL2303 hack also loops over the other interface's bNumEndpoints (line 832).
usbtest's 'e = alt->endpoint + ep' at line 155 is inside a loop bounded by 'for (ep = 0; ep < alt->desc.bNumEndpoints; ep++)' (checked context), so the index is descriptor-count bounded.
mts_usb_probe contains three bNumEndpoints checks (lines 696, 698, 702) validating the interrupt/bulk endpoints before use.

coverage_gaps: drivers/usb/core/{config,devio,driver,hcd,hub,message,devices}.c and drivers/usb/host/xhci.c accesses were only spot-checked for loop-boundedness, not exhaustively re-audited, since they are the descriptor parser itself or internal userspace-API paths.

Files that access endpoint descriptors through cached usb_endpoint_descriptor pointers, usb_pipe_endpoint(), or wrapper macros other than sound/usb get_endpoint were enumerated only via the ->endpoint[ / ->endpoint + / get_endpoint greps; other wrapper names could hide further fixed-index reads.

The ~100 endpoint[]-accessing files with a local bNumEndpoints occurrence were classified by check-position proximity (check line vs use line) rather than by a full data-flow proof for every one; only the highest-risk ones (no check in file, sound/usb, staging, isdn, storage, watchdog, wusbcore, hid, class, serial, image, misc) were read deeply.

drivers/staging trees beyond comedi (dt9812/ni_usb6501/vmk80xx, each with local bNumEndpoints checks), greybus/es2.c, most/hdm-usb, rtl8188eu and drivers/net/can, nfc, irda, bluetooth, media/rc, media/radio, mfd, mmc, i2c, input, w1, uwb consumers were classified from their local bNumEndpoints checks without line-by-line reading.

Whether the OOB-read values (bInterval, wMaxPacketSize, bEndpointAddress) in the three findings can be turned into more than a probe-time crash/DoS (e.g. mis-sized buffers later overflowed) was not traced beyond the immediate sizing/pipe-programming uses named in the reasons.
limitations: No compilation or runtime reproducer was possible (read-only snapshot, no kernel build environment in this run); findings rest on static evidence: grep for bNumEndpoints per file plus complete reading of each probe/bind function named in a finding.

The ueagle-atm finding's OOB-read reachability assumes a gadget can present the Eagle ADSL VID/PIDs with a zero-endpoint interface 0 altsetting 0 while still passing the usbatm bind; this was not verified against the USB core's minimum-endpoint enforcement (none exists for generic interfaces), so it is expressed at high rather than proven-exploitable confidence.

The gigaset finding assumes the M105 USB ID check (VID/PID match) is the only gate; the interface class 255 and altsetting-0 checks were verified in the function, but no device-firmware signing or core-level constraint prevents a malicious gadget from matching them.

sound/usb 6fire, caiaq, hiface, line6, bcd2000, usx2y subdirectories use their own endpoint discovery (e.g. ua101-style or snd_usbmidi paths); they were grepped for endpoint[ patterns and get_endpoint and showed no fixed-index hits, but a wrapper-macro-based access could have been missed.
